regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Support radiotherapy in treating bladder cancer while aiming to preserve the bladder in selected patients.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Mitomycin damages the DNA that dividing cells need. With fluorouracil it helps radiotherapy act against bladder cancer. Healthy marrow and other tissues can also be affected. Fluorouracil, often shortened to 5-FU, interferes with the building blocks used to make DNA and RNA, which cells need to grow. It runs through a vein over the prescribed hours. Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) is an enzyme that breaks it down. Testing for DPD deficiency before treatment reduces risk but cannot rule out every severe reaction.

key_points: NCCP 00450 is the bladder chemoradiation schedule with five-day fluorouracil infusions. Radiotherapy fractions and appointments are prescribed separately; the timeline is an educational reference.

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: EV-301 randomised 608 people previously treated with platinum and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor. Median overall survival was 12.88 months with enfortumab versus 8.97 months with investigator-selected chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% confidence interval 0.56–0.89).
limitations: These group medians do not predict an individual lifespan. The result concerns later-line monotherapy and must not be substituted for evidence about first-line enfortumab/pembrolizumab.
